fun_facts: Austin Simmons played both football and baseball. As a left-handed pitcher, he could throw a fastball up to 94 mph.
At Pahokee High School, he threw for 3,161 yards and 24 touchdowns in his sophomore year.
He graduated high school two years early and earned a 5.3 GPA after taking advanced courses and college-credit classes.
He graduated from Ole Miss with a degree in multidisciplinary studies.
In his 2026 Missouri debut, he completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards and four touchdowns; his 89.5% completion rate was the highest by a quarterback in a Mizzou debut.
In his first four starts for Missouri, he threw 11 touchdown passes—a program mark that surpassed Blaine Gabbert’s total for a Tiger quarterback’s first four starts after his debut.

basis.reasoning: The cited ESPN reporting describes Simmons's football and baseball experience, high-school passing numbers, early graduation and GPA, and Ole Miss degree. The 2026 Missouri notes document his debut performance and the touchdown-pass mark across his first four starts.

excerpts: He's a star football player, one of several elite quarterbacks in the [Ole Miss Rebels](https://www.espn.com/college-football/team/_/id/145/ole-miss-rebels) ' loaded QB room, and a left-handed pitcher who tops out at 94 mph and could have a pro future on the diamond.

He was managing his courses while playing football for Pahokee High School and threw for 3,161 yards, 24 touchdowns and nine interceptions last season -- by age, his sophomore year.

* * *

Despite Simmons' father, David, being a high school football coach, it wasn't until Simmons was 10 that David really thought football would even be an option for him.

At that point, he had fulfilled all his academic requirements and graduated high school. Because he had taken advanced courses and college credits, his grades were worth more than the typical 4.0 scale and he finished with a 5.3 GPA. He was technically still a high school student for athletic eligibility
